block_length_hypothesis: FALSIFIED. At the real count K=500 all blocks 3/5/8 are anticonservative and LONGER blocks are WORSE (26 windows -> ~3 effective blocks at mean-block 8, so win_rate hits extremes more often). The block-length lever fails on this window count.
true_cause: cascade Monte-Carlo noise. The window-block bootstrap does not capture within-forecast MC noise, so two INDEPENDENT K=500 cascade realizations look separated ~11%% of the time at p<0.01. At K=2000 the MC noise is small enough that both axes calibrate clean at block 3.

The one anticonservative regime (independent-MC pairs at K=500) contains only inseparable verdicts, so it is structurally incapable of affecting a registered claim. This is a STRONGER result than a block-length tweak: it is an argument, not a knob.
